title.narrative: Science and policy to manage social change in Central America

description.narrative: UNESCO will strengthen the science-policy nexus through multidisciplinary approaches by operationalizing two MOST Programme workstreams: the UNESCO Inclusive Policy Lab, translating crowdsourced knowledge into inequality-reducing policies through in-country projects and expert workstream contributions; and the HQ–Field Collaboration workstream, connecting regional experts, UNESCO Chairs, and partner networks to global MOST coalitions. Building on its role as Executive Secretariat of CILAC, the office will embed the MOST science-policy agenda as a core pillar of CILAC 2026 (Brasilia, November 2026), connect regional policymakers to MOST global platforms including the Albert Hirschman Lectures and MOST Forum, and organize policy dialogues to build sustained capacity for evidence-based, forward-looking governance.
